job.style: a news-style report about a real-world situation

passage: In the arid regions of Rajasthan, local communities are witnessing a shift in land productivity. While many assume that land degradation is solely the result of sudden natural disasters, the reality is that human activities like overgrazing and excessive irrigation are the primary drivers of soil exhaustion. These activities strip the land of its nutrients, turning fertile fields into barren patches. Interestingly, some villagers mistakenly believe that only living things or moving objects qualify as resources, ignoring that rocks and minerals are vital non-living resources essential for construction and industry. Furthermore, there is a common debate regarding the status of human-made infrastructure like canals. Some argue that these are not 'real' resources because they are man-made, yet these structures are critical for managing water, which is a renewable resource. However, even renewable resources require careful management. A dangerous misconception persists that because water is renewable, it will never run out regardless of how much we consume. This belief leads to reckless water usage, ignoring the fact that replenishment rates are often slower than our current consumption levels. Sustainable development requires us to recognize that all resources, whether natural or human-made, must be utilized with foresight to ensure they remain available for future generations.

items.evidence: While many assume that land degradation is solely the result of sudden natural disasters, the reality is that human activities like overgrazing and excessive irrigation are the primary drivers of soil exhaustion.
items.q: A Rajasthan village has had no floods, yet its fields turn barren. What is the likely cause?
options: Overgrazing and heavy watering stripped the soil
Floods from earlier years damaged the soil
Digging out rocks and minerals stripped the soil
Dry weather alone drained the soil of nutrients
items.explain: Human activities like overgrazing and excessive irrigation are the main drivers of soil exhaustion, not only disasters.

wrong.why: thinks land degradation comes only from natural disasters
blames an activity the passage does not name as a cause
blames the dry climate instead of human activity

items.evidence: Interestingly, some villagers mistakenly believe that only living things or moving objects qualify as resources, ignoring that rocks and minerals are vital non-living resources essential for construction and industry.
items.q: A villager says a stone is no resource because it neither moves nor lives. Why is that wrong?
options: Non-living materials are resources if people can use them
Stones become resources only once they start moving
Only plants and animals can serve industry and building
Stones count only after they are shaped into products
items.explain: Rocks and minerals are non-living, yet they are vital resources for construction and industry.

wrong.why: thinks only things that move or live are resources
thinks industry can use only living things
thinks a material is a resource only after processing

items.evidence: Some argue that these are not 'real' resources because they are man-made, yet these structures are critical for managing water, which is a renewable resource.
items.q: Why is a canal called a resource although people built it?
options: It is useful for managing the water supply
It was first formed by nature, then changed
Man-made things are resources only in a lesser sense
It carries renewable water, so it is renewable too
items.explain: Canals are critical for managing water, so they count as real resources even though they are man-made.

wrong.why: thinks only natural things can be resources
thinks human-made resources are not really resources
mixes up the canal with the water it carries

items.evidence: This belief leads to reckless water usage, ignoring the fact that replenishment rates are often slower than our current consumption levels.
items.q: Why can a renewable resource like water still run short?
options: People may use it faster than it refills
Used water turns non-renewable once it is polluted
Water takes very long to form, so it ends
Canals made by people stop it from refilling
items.explain: Replenishment is often slower than our consumption, so even renewable water can run out.

wrong.why: thinks used or polluted water cannot come back
thinks slow formation makes a resource non-renewable
blames human-made structures, not the rate of use

items.evidence: Sustainable development requires us to recognize that all resources, whether natural or human-made, must be utilized with foresight to ensure they remain available for future generations.
items.q: What does sustainable development ask us to do with resources?
options: Use them wisely so later people can have them
Leave them untouched so nothing is ever used
Use only natural ones and avoid man-made ones
Use renewable ones freely since they never end
items.explain: All resources must be used with foresight so they stay available for future generations.

wrong.why: thinks conservation means not using a resource at all
thinks human-made resources do not really count
thinks renewable resources never run out
